newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha dips, contango deeper on high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha dips, contango deeper on high stocks.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices slipped on Monday, while the contango in near-term spreads continued to broaden due to slack end-user demand, traders said on Monday.
Second-half July/second-half August was notionally quoted at minus $2.50/minus $1.00 after trading at minus $1.75 on Friday.
Earlier last week, the spread changed hands at even.
End-user demand for prompt cargoes was depressed because of high inventories, traders said.
Stocks were particularly high at petrochemical firms located in Chiba, near Tokyo, they said.
"At least one vessel is floating off the coast because there is no storage tank space available," one trader said.
As of end-April, Japan's naphtha stock levels were 20 percent higher than those a year ago.
Open-spec naphtha first-half August was assessed at $212.00/213.00 per tonne, down about $1.00 from late Friday levels. Second-half August was quoted about 50 cents higher than first-half August.
